title.narrative: Rendering Educational and Vocational assistance to Ebola orphans and young persons in Western Rural

description.narrative:
There has been an unprecedented outbreak of the Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Sierra Leone. Since the outbreak of EVD in May 2014, local partners and the Government of Sierra Leone conducted Ebola sensitization and awareness raising campaigns. These covered messages on the prevention and control of the spread of Ebola in various communities in the north. In communities hit by Ebola and poverty, there are hundreds of children/ young persons who may not be orphans, but who have been made more vulnerable by Ebola thus becoming Ebola victims. In addition to informal needs assessments based on field observation and community consultation, the protection and livelihood needs of Ebola victims/orphans, have been identified through consultations and Focus Group Discussions held by our field officers. For example, children whose parents were ill with Ebola might not receive the care and support they require.
Orphans and vulnerable children have many different needs; for love, security, attention, health, shelter, nutrition and many others. One of the most important needs that orphans have is education. Education is a basic human right for all children, as recognized in the Convention on the Rights of the Child. A child who has access to quality primary schooling has a better chance in life. A child who knows how to read, write and do basic arithmetic has a solid foundation for continued learning throughout life. Education is critically important to children’s social integration and psychosocial well-being. School attendance helps children affected by trauma to regain a sense of normalcy and to recover from the psychosocial impacts of their experiences and disrupted lives. However, the effects of the EVD outbreak on children in Sierra Leone have been catastrophic, depriving them the opportunity to access this basic human right. The project plans to offer assistance in providing livelihood support and education support to target beneficiaries. Livelihood support will consist of providing apprenticeship/ attachment to life skill training centres for carpentry, welding, masoning, tailoring and gara tie dying and working tools will be provided for beneficiaries. On the other hand, education support will consist of proving school fees, uniforms and a school kit which includes books, , pens and pencil, and ceremonial uniforms etc. This is geared to help beneficiaries regain lost dignity and alleviate their poverty level, which is a major pillar of CAFOD intervention strategies in poor communities. The assessment of the beneficiaries needs was based on consultations and focus group discussions held last year with chiefdom authorities and including vulnerable members of the community especially women, disabled, children and Ebola victims’ families since they were in a better place to know and identify Ebola victims and those in desperate needs or rather most vulnerable or poorest of the poor.
